captions.text: So I want to talk about how I got diagnosed with narcolepsy because honestly nobody believes me when I tell this story.
The thing that finally made me go to a doctor was I fell asleep driving. Not for long. Maybe two seconds.
But I drifted into the next lane and a guy honked at me and I pulled over and sat there shaking for twenty minutes.
I fell asleep in under three minutes every single time. And I went straight into REM, which you are not supposed to do.
That is the diagnosis right there. That is narcolepsy. Your brain skips the queue and goes straight to dreaming.
When the doctor told me, I did not feel sad. I felt relieved. Genuinely relieved. Because it meant I was not lazy.
I had spent six years thinking I had a character problem. It was a neurological condition the whole time.
But then I started falling asleep in conversations. Mid sentence. Someone would be talking to me and I would just go.
I thought I was just tired. I genuinely thought for two years that I was just a tired person and that was my personality.
So I go to my doctor and I say I think something is wrong with me and she says you are probably just stressed.
And I want to be clear, I am not mad at her. That is what it looks like. A tired college kid saying he is tired.
But I pushed. I said no, I fell asleep at the wheel, this is not normal tired. And she referred me to a sleep clinic.
When the doctor told me, I did not feel sad. I felt relieved. Genuinely relieved. Because it meant I was not lazy.
I had spent six years thinking I had a character problem. It was a neurological condition the whole time.

options.title: The test that gave me an answer

captions.text: The sleep study is the strangest night of your life. They glue about thirty electrodes to your head and say, okay, sleep naturally.
Then the next day they do what is called a nap study. They put you in a dark room five times and tell you to try to sleep.
A normal person takes fifteen, twenty minutes to fall asleep in that situation. If they fall asleep at all.
